identity: A secondary-school biology question bank (Jordanian/Egyptian style), 20 four-option items on one layout line each: plant cell walls, placental hormones, DNA structural units, bean-plant movements, spindle fibres, the terminal electron acceptor, contraception, Chargaff base counting, anaphase, the Calvin cycle (asked twice, once with PGAL and once with G-3-P), physiological support, starfish reproduction, muscle types, oogenesis, joints, peristalsis, mitosis in unicellular organisms, deer competition, and pineapple vs apple fruit. Latin-script chemistry survives untranslated (CO 2, NADPH, ATP, G 3 P, IH), and the scan is scarred: 'تكو ن' for 'تكوّن' @127, 'ع' for 'على' @252, 'ب ن' for 'بين' @367/381/386, 'الإقل م' for 'الإقليمي' @378, and a stray 'SEG ج' at @237.
law: §S. 20 lines × [stem ‖ opt ‖ opt ‖ opt ‖ opt] = 100 boundaries over 419 tokens (4.2 tokens/segment). Stems end at the last token the options share — usually a copula or preposition (هي @33، من @60، هو @73/@109/@284، بعملية @222، بأنها @375، ماعدا @23، ترسيب @6) or the last word of a full question (فأي العبارات الآتية صحيحة @151/@192، بهذا الاسم @324، بين الأسنان @306). Nothing inside a stem cuts however long the stem runs: item 8's 18-token Chargaff set-up with its وكان clause, and items 10/11's 13- and 15-token إذا-conditionals, are each ONE segment (S1).
reasoning:
Chemistry and OCR debris were the two things that could have broken the option count, and both are protected sites:
- 'CO 2' (@156-157, @197-198) is CO₂ split by subscript stripping — A2, never cut inside a formula. Same for 'G 3 P' inside the stem @186-188. If I had cut there, items 10 and 11 would have shown five and six options against every other item's four.
- 'تكو ن' (@127-128), 'ع' (@252), 'ب ن' (@367 @381 @386), 'الإقل م' (@378-379) are OCR breakages of single words — LAW 0''' item 3, weld. Note 'تنافس ب ن الأنواع المختلفة' and 'تنافس ب ن النوع الواحد' are two five-token options, not four two-token ones.
- 'SEG ج' @237: the same pipeline artifact gold kept inside a segment in doc_46717e5891d4 ('… اجتماعية ‖ SEG د اقتصاد يه و عسكرية ‖') and that I handled correctly in doc_c4cb5672fc6c this batch. SEG opens the option, the letter ج welds to its text, so option 3 of the starfish item is the whole 'SEG ج لا جنسى بالتوالد البكرى الصناعى' @237-243.
Items 10 and 11 are the same question asked twice with PGAL and G-3-P (the same molecule under two names), and their four options are word-for-word identical. That parallelism is my strongest structural check in the document: the two option sets must split identically, and they do — @157/@198, @165/@206, @170/@211, @176/@217.
Catch-all options are single segments: 'جميع الإجابات صحيحة' (item 1), 'جميع الإجابات السابقة صحيحة' (13), 'جميع الإجابات السابقة خاطئة' (16), 'أخر إجابتين' (4), 'كل انواع العضلات' (14) — recovered entry 7.
My one genuinely uncertain call is item 4, @45. The stem could end at 'به' (@44), making the options 'حركة اللمس / نوم ويقظة / حركة إنتحاء / أخر إجابتين', or at 'حركة' (@45), making them 'اللمس / نوم ويقظة / حركة إنتحاء / أخر إجابتين'. The word حركة is printed twice, at @45 and again inside option 3 at @49, which is evidence against factoring it out. But the batch-12 refinement is explicit that a head printed ONCE in prefix position belongs to the stem (doc_87ac286b6785: 'يصنع الصابون من زيت ‖ الزيتون ‖'), and 'حركة إنتحاء' is a different category term (tropism) rather than a third member of a 'حركة + X' series. I take @45. Medium; the alternative costs exactly one boundary.
Check: all 19 pre-<NL> tokens plus @418 fall out of the option structure with no forcing, which is what tells me none of the 20 items was mis-split.
